summary: Env tag normalizer strips 'env_namespace' attribute causing JIT/ephemeral access failure across AWS/GCP
description:
Issue summary:
Platform's env-tag normalizer service recently started dropping the 'env_namespace' attribute from session metadata created by the JIT provisioning flow. This causes downstream AWS STS/GCP IAM conditional policies to fail authorization checks during cross-cloud ephemeral access (dedicated sandbox/jit).

Impact:
- JIT sandbox provisioning fails for ~12% of developer/service-seat requests in prod/us-east-1 and ~8% in staging/us-west-2 since 2026-03-09 03:00 UTC.
- Affected jobs fail with AssumeRoleDenied / PERMISSION_DENIED (IAM Condition) errors and block debugging and onboarding flows for platform teams.
- Workload impact: CI jobs, ephemeral notebooks, and ad-hoc debugging sessions that rely on cross-account/service-account impersonation.

Environment:
- service: env-tag-normalizer v1.4.2 (k8s cluster: infra-core-prod, infra-core-staging)
- Affected auth flows: jit-provisioner -> service-broker -> aws-sts (assume-role) and gcp-iam (serviceAccount:generateAccessToken)
- Time window: Starts ~2026-03-09 03:00 UTC after a config rollout of normalization rules.

Steps to reproduce (non-customer):
1. Trigger JIT provisioning (internal endpoint) for a sandbox with env_namespace="dev-team-42" and tags: {service: "notebook"}.
2. Inspect the session metadata emitted by env-tag-normalizer (k8s logs / emitted JSON).
3. Attempt aws:sts:AssumeRole with SessionTags containing env_namespace and observe AssumeRoleDenied or role mismatch.
4. Attempt gcloud iam service-accounts generate-access-token with IAM Condition referencing request.auth.claims.env_namespace; observe PERMISSION_DENIED.

Observed errors/snippets:
- AWS STS: "Client.UnauthorizedOperation: The session tags provided do not match expected tags." correlated with assume-role ID arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/ops-broker/foobar
- GCP IAM: "PERMISSION_DENIED: Condition check failed: request.auth.claims.env_namespace is missing" in audit logs.

Initial hypothesis:
The new normalization rule (PR #4221) collapses/filters attributes considered 'non-standard', and 'env_namespace' was erroneously classified. The normalizer strips the attribute before the session is packaged and signed. Downstream identity broker logic expects that attribute for conditional IAM bindings, so its absence triggers denies.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a dev sandbox request with env_namespace set. 2) Watch env-tag-normalizer pod logs for the emitted session payload. 3) Attempt assume-role/generate-access-token using the JIT token and observe authorization failure. 4) Compare payloads before and after normalizer (pre-rollout snapshot available in S3).
investigation_notes: 2026-03-09 03:12 UTC - Alerts: increased rate of AssumeRoleDenied in prod (pager). Notified oncall-sre (#oncall).
Checked recent deploys: env-tag-normalizer config map rolled out 2026-03-09 02:58 UTC via infra CI (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4221).
Replayed one failing request against a pre-rollout snapshot of the normalizer and confirmed env_namespace present in payload -> downstream assume-role succeeds.
Replayed same request against current normalizer and payload shows env_namespace removed from 'session_tags' array. Downstream assume-role fails with tag mismatch.
GCP audit logs show IAM Condition failure citing missing request.auth.claims.env_namespace, matching AWS symptom (policy gating based on same attribute).
Temporary workaround (applied 2026-03-09 04:30 UTC): reverted config map to previous normalization rules in prod (hotfix) which immediately reduced failure rate to baseline.
Root cause appears to be a rule in config that trims attributes matching regex /^env_.*/ if length > 16; env_namespace triggered a false positive because of internal prefix mapping.
comments: Ava Martinez (2026-03-09 03:20 UTC): Observed spike in assume-role denies tied to JIT flow. Opening ticket and rolling this up to SRE and Auth teams.
SRE Pager (2026-03-09 03:35 UTC): Reverted normalization config in prod as immediate mitigation. Failures dropped from 12% -> 1% within two minutes. Need a patch rather than full rollback.

Ravi Singh (Assignee) (2026-03-09 06:10 UTC): Patch in progress to adjust normalization rule to whitelist env_namespace and any attribute referenced by IAM Conditions via the 'iam_condition_whitelist'. Will test in staging before deploy to prod.

Security (Maya Patel) (2026-03-09 09:05 UTC): Confirmed this attribute is allowed from a security/privacy perspective. Approving whitelist for env_namespace and env_owner for now. Recommend audit of normalization rules for other ATTR/CLAIM names used by policies.
Platform (2026-03-10 11:22 UTC): Created PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4234 with unit tests against a matrix of claim names; staging test passed 2026-03-10 18:00 UTC.
Ravi Singh (2026-03-13 10:03 UTC): Rolling patch to prod tonight after maintenance window. Will include a follow-up cleanup task to centralize claim->policy mapping in config.
next_steps: 1) Deploy PR #4234 to prod in controlled window (2026-03-14 02:00 UTC). 2) Add automated integration test that validates session metadata contains all attributes referenced by active IAM Conditions. 3) Run a config audit to map normalization rules to SIMS of IAM Conditions (owner: Security). 4) Create runbook entry for emergency rollback and mitigation steps.
resolution: Mitigation: config rollback applied 2026-03-09 (hotfix) restored service. Long-term fix: whitelist-based normalization rule merged in PR #4234; scheduled deploy to prod 2026-03-14. Post-deploy will monitor assume-role and IAM Condition failure rates for 24h. Follow-up: add automated gating that cross-checks normalization whitelist against IAM policies.
workaround: Reverted env-tag-normalizer to previous config (prior to PR #4221). For teams needing immediate access, platform ops can manually create temporary session tags via ops-broker until patch is live.
postmortem_action_items: Create integration test: verify normalization output contains attributes referenced by IAM Conditions (owner: auth team).
Add a pre-deploy validation step to infra CI that compares normalization whitelist against live IAM Condition attribute inventory (owner: security).
Document env attribute naming conventions and publish to Confluence (owner: platform).
Schedule a 1-week audit to find other normalization rules that may affect cross-cloud policies (owner: auth + sec).
